rules.title: Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces the 1961 Act
rules.summary: The Income-tax Act, 2025 applies from 1 April 2026 (tax year 2026-27). 'Previous year' and 'assessment year' are replaced by a single 'tax year'. Income earned in 2025-26 is still governed by the 1961 Act and filed as AY 2026-27.
rules.keywords: new act old act tax year assessment year previous year renumbered sections

rules.title: New tax regime is the default
rules.summary: The new regime is the default for individuals. It has lower slab rates but allows only a few deductions (standard deduction, employer NPS contribution). Salaried people can choose the old regime each year when filing; people with business income can switch back only once.
rules.keywords: new regime default opt out old regime choose switch 115bac 202

rules.title: New regime slab rates
rules.summary: 0–4 lakh: nil; 4–8 lakh: 5%; 8–12 lakh: 10%; 12–16 lakh: 15%; 16–20 lakh: 20%; 20–24 lakh: 25%; above 24 lakh: 30%. Same for all ages.
rules.keywords: slab rates new regime tax rates brackets

rules.title: Old regime slab rates
rules.summary: Below 60: 0–2.5 lakh nil, 2.5–5 lakh 5%, 5–10 lakh 20%, above 10 lakh 30%. Seniors (60–79): nil up to 3 lakh. Super seniors (80+): nil up to 5 lakh, 5–10 lakh 20%.

citation.2025-26: First Schedule / Finance Act, Income-tax Act, 1961 regime
citation.2026-27: Rates for the old regime under Income-tax Act, 2025 (Finance Act 2026)

rules.keywords: old regime slabs senior citizen super senior basic exemption

rules.title: Standard deduction for salary and pension
rules.summary: Salaried employees and pensioners get a flat standard deduction: ₹75,000 in the new regime and ₹50,000 in the old regime.

citation.2026-27: Income-tax Act, 2025 — provision corresponding to s.16(ia) of the 1961 Act (confirm the new section number)

rules.keywords: standard deduction salary pension 75000 50000

rules.title: Rebate — no tax up to ₹12 lakh (new regime)
rules.summary: Resident individuals pay no tax in the new regime if total income is up to ₹12 lakh (rebate up to ₹60,000), with marginal relief just above ₹12 lakh. In the old regime the rebate is up to ₹12,500 for income up to ₹5 lakh. The rebate does not apply to tax on special-rate income such as capital gains under s.111A/112A.
rules.keywords: rebate 87a 156 12 lakh tax free zero tax marginal relief

rules.title: Investments and payments deduction (80C) — ₹1.5 lakh
rules.summary: Old regime only. Up to ₹1,50,000 a year for EPF, PPF, ELSS, life-insurance premium, principal repayment of a home loan, children's tuition fees, 5-year tax-saving FD, NSC, Sukanya Samriddhi and similar.
rules.keywords: 80c 123 ppf elss epf lic tuition principal tax saving fd nsc ssy deduction limit

rules.title: NPS deductions
rules.summary: Own NPS contribution: extra ₹50,000 over the 80C limit (old regime, s.80CCD(1B)). Employer's NPS contribution: deductible up to 14% of salary in the new regime and 10% in the old regime.
rules.keywords: nps 80ccd 1b employer contribution 124 50000

rules.title: Health insurance deduction (80D)
rules.summary: Old regime only. Health-insurance premium: up to ₹25,000 for self/spouse/children (₹50,000 if a senior citizen) plus up to ₹25,000 for parents (₹50,000 if they are senior). Preventive health check-ups up to ₹5,000 fall within these limits.
rules.keywords: 80d 126 health insurance medical premium parents senior mediclaim

rules.title: Education loan interest (80E)
rules.summary: Old regime only. The full interest on a loan for higher education of self, spouse or children is deductible, with no upper limit, for up to 8 years from when repayment starts.
rules.keywords: 80e 129 education loan interest student loan

rules.title: Donations (80G)
rules.summary: Old regime only. Donations to approved funds and charities are deductible at 50% or 100%, some subject to a limit of 10% of adjusted income. Cash donations above ₹2,000 do not qualify.
rules.keywords: 80g 133 donation charity

rules.title: Interest on savings and deposits (80TTA / 80TTB)
rules.summary: Old regime only. Savings-account interest up to ₹10,000 is deductible (80TTA). Senior citizens can deduct up to ₹50,000 of interest on savings accounts and deposits (80TTB).
rules.keywords: 80tta 80ttb 153 savings interest fd interest senior

rules.title: Home-loan interest on a self-occupied house
rules.summary: Old regime only. Interest on a loan for a self-occupied house is deductible up to ₹2,00,000 a year (construction must finish within 5 years). For a let-out house the interest is fully deductible from rent, but the overall house-property loss that can be set off against other income is capped at ₹2,00,000. The new regime allows no deduction for a self-occupied house.

citation.2026-27: Income-tax Act, 2025 — provision corresponding to s.24(b) of the 1961 Act (confirm the new section number)

rules.keywords: home loan interest 24b house property self occupied let out loss

rules.title: House rent allowance (HRA) exemption
rules.summary: Old regime only. The exempt part of HRA is the lowest of: actual HRA received; rent paid minus 10% of basic salary (+DA); 50% of basic salary in Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata or Chennai (40% elsewhere). Landlord PAN is needed if rent exceeds ₹1 lakh a year.

citation.2026-27: Income-tax Act, 2025 — provision corresponding to s.10(13A) of the 1961 Act (confirm the new section number)

rules.keywords: hra house rent allowance rent exemption metro basic salary

rules.title: Short-term gains on listed shares and equity funds
rules.summary: Gains on STT-paid listed shares and equity mutual funds held 12 months or less are taxed at 20% (plus surcharge and cess). The rebate does not apply to this tax.
rules.keywords: stcg short term capital gains shares equity mutual fund 111a 196 20%

rules.title: Long-term gains on listed shares and equity funds
rules.summary: Gains on STT-paid listed shares and equity mutual funds held more than 12 months are taxed at 12.5% on the amount above ₹1.25 lakh a year.
rules.keywords: ltcg long term capital gains shares equity 112a 198 12.5% 1.25 lakh exemption

rules.title: Long-term gains on property, gold and other assets
rules.summary: Other long-term gains are taxed at 12.5% without indexation (property and unlisted assets held over 24 months). For land or buildings bought before 23 July 2024, resident individuals may instead pay 20% with indexation if that is lower.

citation.2026-27: Income-tax Act, 2025 — provision corresponding to s.112 of the 1961 Act (confirm the new section number)

rules.keywords: ltcg property gold real estate indexation 112 12.5% 20%

rules.title: Surcharge and cess
rules.summary: Surcharge applies above ₹50 lakh (10%), ₹1 crore (15%), ₹2 crore (25%) and ₹5 crore (37%; capped at 25% in the new regime). Surcharge on listed-equity capital gains is capped at 15%. Health and education cess is 4% on tax plus surcharge.
rules.keywords: surcharge cess health education 4% high income

rules.title: Advance tax instalments
rules.summary: Pay advance tax if the year's tax after TDS is ₹10,000 or more: at least 15% by 15 June, 45% by 15 September, 75% by 15 December and 100% by 15 March. Resident senior citizens without business income are exempt. Presumptive-tax (44AD/44ADA) taxpayers can pay everything by 15 March.

citation.2026-27: Income-tax Act, 2025 — provision corresponding to s.208–211 of the 1961 Act (confirm the new section number)

rules.keywords: advance tax instalment due date june september december march 10000

rules.title: Interest for late return or short advance tax
rules.summary: Simple interest of 1% a month applies for filing the return late when tax is unpaid (234A), for paying less than 90% of tax as advance tax (234B) and for missing instalments (234C). A late-filing fee of ₹5,000 (₹1,000 if income is up to ₹5 lakh) also applies.

citation.2026-27: Income-tax Act, 2025 — provision corresponding to s.234A/234B/234C/234F of the 1961 Act (confirm the new section number)

rules.keywords: interest 234a 234b 234c 234f late fee penalty delay

rules.title: Return due dates — income earned in 2025-26
rules.summary: For income of 2025-26 (AY 2026-27): 31 July 2026 for individuals not needing an audit (ITR-1/ITR-2); 31 August 2026 for non-audit ITR-3/ITR-4; 31 October 2026 for audit cases. A belated or revised return can be filed until 31 December 2026 (a belated return pays the late fee and loses some loss carry-forwards).
rules.keywords: itr due date last date file return belated revised deadline july august

rules.title: Return of income under the new Act
rules.summary: From tax year 2026-27 the obligation to file a return is in section 263 of the Income-tax Act, 2025. Due dates for income earned in 2026-27 will fall in 2027; confirm them when notified.
rules.keywords: return of income 263 139 filing obligation

rules.title: Presumptive income for small business and professionals
rules.summary: Small businesses can declare 8% of turnover as profit (6% for digital receipts) if turnover is up to ₹2 crore (₹3 crore when cash receipts are at most 5%). Specified professionals can declare 50% of receipts if receipts are up to ₹50 lakh (₹75 lakh when cash receipts are at most 5%).

citation.2026-27: Income-tax Act, 2025 — provision corresponding to s.44AD/44ADA of the 1961 Act (confirm the new section number)

rules.keywords: presumptive 44ad 44ada freelancer small business professional turnover

rules.title: TDS on salary
rules.summary: Employers deduct tax from salary each month at the average rate for the estimated yearly tax, using the regime the employee chooses. Form 16 summarises it.
rules.keywords: tds salary form 16 employer deduction 192 392

rules.title: TDS on deposit interest
rules.summary: Banks deduct 10% TDS on deposit interest above ₹50,000 a year (₹1 lakh for senior citizens); 20% if PAN is missing. Form 15G/15H can be submitted when the total income is below the taxable limit.
rules.keywords: tds fd interest 194a 393 15g 15h bank deposit

rules.title: Fair treatment by lenders and recovery agents
rules.summary: RBI rules require lenders and their recovery agents to act fairly: no threats, abuse or public humiliation, and no recovery calls before 8 am or after 7 pm. The lender is responsible for its agents.

citation.all: RBI directions on outsourcing / recovery agents (August 2022) and Fair Practices Code

rules.keywords: recovery agent harassment calls threat rbi fair practice collection

rules.title: Complaints against banks and lenders
rules.summary: Complain to the lender first. If there is no reply within 30 days or the answer is unsatisfactory, file a free complaint with the RBI Integrated Ombudsman at cms.rbi.org.in (or call 14448).
rules.keywords: complaint ombudsman rbi grievance bank nbfc cms

rules.title: No prepayment penalty on floating-rate loans
rules.summary: Banks and NBFCs cannot charge foreclosure or prepayment penalties on floating-rate term loans taken by individuals for non-business purposes, such as most home loans.

citation.all: RBI circulars on foreclosure charges for floating-rate loans

rules.keywords: prepayment penalty foreclosure charges floating rate home loan part payment

rules.title: Credit-card minimum due and billing
rules.summary: Under RBI's credit-card directions, the minimum amount due must be set so that the balance does not keep growing (no negative amortisation), and issuers cannot charge interest on interest-free-period amounts that are paid in full. Paying only the minimum still costs very high interest.

citation.all: RBI (Credit Card and Debit Card – Issuance and Conduct) Directions, 2022

rules.keywords: credit card minimum due interest free period billing rbi

rules.title: Mental-health support line
rules.summary: Tele-MANAS is India's free, 24×7 national mental-health helpline: 14416 (or 1-800-891-4416).

citation.all: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare – Tele-MANAS

rules.keywords: stress anxiety depression helpline suicide mental health

rules.title: Which ITR form to use (income of 2025-26)
rules.summary: ITR-1 (Sahaj): resident individuals with total income up to ₹50 lakh from salary/pension, up to two house properties, interest and similar income, listed-equity LTCG up to ₹1.25 lakh (no carried-forward loss) and agricultural income up to ₹5,000. Not for directors, unlisted shareholders, foreign assets, crypto, business income or larger capital gains. ITR-2: other capital gains, more properties or foreign income without business income. ITR-3: business or professional income. ITR-4: presumptive business income with total income up to ₹50 lakh.

citation.2025-26: Section 139 and ITR forms notified for AY 2026-27, Income-tax Act, 1961

rules.keywords: itr form itr-1 sahaj itr-2 itr-3 itr-4 sugam which form eligibility

rules.title: Cost Inflation Index (indexation)
rules.summary: CII values (base 2001-02 = 100): 2010-11: 167, 2015-16: 254, 2020-21: 301, 2023-24: 348, 2024-25: 363, 2025-26: 376, 2026-27: 384. Indexation now applies only to the optional 20% rate for land or buildings bought before 23 July 2024.

citation.all: CBDT notifications on the Cost Inflation Index

rules.keywords: cost inflation index cii indexation indexed cost property

rules.title: Saving tax on property gains by reinvesting
rules.summary: Long-term gains on a house can be exempt if reinvested in another residential house (s.54, up to ₹10 crore) or in specified bonds within 6 months (s.54EC, up to ₹50 lakh). Gains on other long-term assets can be exempt if the net sale value is invested in a house (s.54F). Conditions on timing and lock-in apply.

citation.2026-27: Income-tax Act, 2025 — provisions corresponding to ss.54/54EC/54F of the 1961 Act (confirm the new section numbers)

rules.keywords: 54 54ec 54f reinvest capital gains exemption bonds house
